# Regex Anchors: `^` and `$`

**`^`** matches the **start of a string** (or line, in multiline mode).

**`$`** matches the **end of a string** (or line, in multiline mode).

## Examples

| Pattern | Matches | Doesn't match |
|---------|---------|---------------|
| `^hello` | `hello world` | `say hello` |
| `world$` | `hello world` | `world peace` |
| `^world$` | `world` | `hello world`, `world!` |
| `^[A-Z]` | `Apple pie` | `apple pie` |
| `\d+$` | `abc123` | `123abc` |

## Multiline Mode

In **single-line mode** (default), `^` and `$` match only the string boundaries.

In **multiline mode** (flag: `m` or `(?m)`), they match line boundaries instead:

```regex
^foo  # matches "foo" at the start of any line
bar$  # matches "bar" at the end of any line
```

Example in JavaScript:
```javascript
const text = "foo\nbar\nbaz";
/^bar$/m.test(text);  // true (bar is on its own line)
/^bar$/.test(text);   // false (bar is not the entire string)
```

## Common Patterns

- `^[A-Z]` — string starts with uppercase letter
- `\w+@\w+\.\w+$` — basic email validation
- `^$` — matches empty string or blank line
